target_customer: Defense technology companies and contractors serving the Department of War and special operations that must run AI on premises
problem: Defense teams cannot send sensitive data to cloud AI and need compliant local compute. BayMachines sizes, configures and installs air gapped GPU systems built to support CMMC and NIST 800-171.
business_model: Hardware and managed deployment sales (AI Box, GPU Server, Private Cluster)
product_category: On premise air gapped AI compute for defense

competitors.name: EdgeRunner AI
competitors.what: Air gapped on device AI agents for military and enterprise

technical_complexity.rationale: Assembling and configuring GPU systems with open weight models and compliance documentation is mostly integration work with compliance parts.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance know how and defense relationships help, but turnkey GPU vendors such as VRLA Tech and PackScale market the same offering.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; vendor marketing pages show established small rivals.

market_need_then: Defense teams need local AI under CMMC and ITAR rules, and cloud use is restricted for sensitive data. The site lists five logos it does not label as customers.

branding.domain_note: Uses baymachines.com, an exact match .com. Acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Air-gapped compute for American defense.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; name resembles local machine shops such as Bay Machine and Fabrication.

outcome_analysis: BayMachines is an Active Spring 2026 YC company with seven staff selling air gapped GPU systems to defense teams. Founders were not found on its YC page or site, no verified funding exists, and several turnkey rivals sell the same thing, so the outcome is open.
notes: Founders left empty because neither the YC page nor the website names them; Dealroom lists CEO Kerim Taray and CTO Andres Garza, an unverified aggregator source. Dealroom also lists a 125K USD seed with no investors and no second source, so not recorded as a round. Outcome search returned nothing about the company. Completeness pass: the seed round rests on a single database (Dealroom, $125K, no investors or date). Press search found nothing about the company; the Bay security startup that raised $50M is a different company.
